I don’t honestly know where to start.

I joined this surgery a few months back. My first appointment which was booked with a gp ended up being a nurse. This appointment was to get my medications sorted with being new to the practice.

In the appointment this nurse repeatedly asked how much alcohol I drink on a daily basis. When I told her I don’t drink often, only really on special occasions unless I take a little fancy to have a strongbow every now and again. She wouldn’t take my answer. Instead she said well when you walked into the room all she could smell was drink. She said I don’t think you’re being honest with me.

My next appointment was great as the doctor I was seeing was only at the surgery for a few days but he Fully understood my conditions and was willing to go above and beyond to help.

He put me on morphine patches to help with pain. We agreed that my conditions are never going to go away but instead will only get worse as I get older. He advised me to stick with these patches for a month and then to call back to get them increased and that he would keep doing this until the pain was well managed.

So I’ve been on the patched a month and as agreed I called up. Requested a phone appointment with the gp.  I waited all day for this call. When I received the call it was from an extremely rude nurse. When I told her I was just needing my patches increased she said I’m not doing that.  You’re on a lot of medication I would rather take you off your medication.

Now giving the fact I used to be on 35 tablets a day and now I am on 5. I don’t think I’m on a lot of medication. Again I was asked repeatedly how much alcohol I drink. Then she proceeded to ask what drugs I take. I told her just what was on my prescription to which she replied no. What drugs do you do.

She constantly talked over the top of me and when I stopped her from doing this telling her the call would not be productive if she treated me this way and  if she continues to treat me this way she would need to pass me on to someone who will listen. She said there is no one else here and hung up.

I called the surgery and spoke to the receptionist who is always lovely (Julie). She managed to sort out that a few extra patches would be given until the doctor could call me back.

I came off that phone call with a huge fibro and crps flare up due to the stress. My pain levels went through the roof. All because of a stupid and ignorant.

Later that day the same nurse calls me to tell me that she has issues a few patches to see me through to Monday when a doctor would call me.

Skipping ahead a few days I received my blister pack from the pharmacy. Not thinking that anything else would be different I took my meds as normal.

What followed was horrible. I was up all night with hallucinations, severe panic attacks, heart palpitations, flashbacks of previous trauma, severe sweats and a PTSD trigger.  I was up all night not knowing where I was or what was happening to me.

The next day I went to work. At around 11am my pharmacist called me to see how I was getting on with my blister pack. I explained how I was feeling and when the pharmacist looked up my list of medications it soon became clear what the issue was.

The nurse at Eastmoor surgery had clearly taken issue with me as a patient standing up to her. She had issued all my old medications at the highest doses. No wonder I was having these side affects. The pharmacist told me that I shouldn’t be driving. I needed to go home and call a doctor for an appointment immediately.

It turns out that the mixture of the high dose medication along with being on morphine patches causes a severe overdose of pain relief. A reaction that could have led to sudden death syndrome.

Since this happens in may. I haven’t been myself. I am still unable to take my meds as prescribed. I have made a formal complaint to the surgery however I’ve been fobbed off in every way. Several months of ignored emails and to top it all off a new manager who is practice is appalling. I’m not sure if the gps are part time but I can never get an appointment. They use an NHS internal system where medical professionals are supposed to communicate with each other, however I ended up having my stent procedure delayed significantly as they advised they’d not received correspondence when it was very clear they had. It took the consultants secretary at LGI to contact them directly before they admitted they’d got it wrong whilst my condition deteriorated rapidly at this time. One of the GPs didn’t read a simple report properly and as a result, until I managed to get an appointment with an advanced nurse practitioner, I put up with months of pain. I was then unable to get the right pain medication as 2 gps disagreed with each other leaving me unable to sleep for weeks and function properly. My works occupational health were disgusted and so was my heart consultant. To be fair to the I’ve found receptionists Julie and Kay very helpful and appreciate they’re up against it. The ANP and nurse who takes bloods are lovely but  if you have the misfortune to get one of their colleagues, who is a receptionist, she’s rude, dismissive, obstructive and has even been sarcastic towards me. When I challenged her about this politely, rather than apologise, she said that everyone has off days but she seems to be having an off day every time I’ve been unfortunate enough to speak to her. The practise is poorly run and managed in my opinion and despite writing a complaint to the practice manager several months ago, I’ve had no response. Following a heart procedure my consultant and rehab nurse used the system to tell them I need rigorous checks including regular bloods.
